title: Nitrogen-sensitive ectomycorrhizal fungi did not clearly recover where deposition fell in British records, 1986-2025; a post-hoc nitrogen index followed deposition for ECM fungi, not saprotrophs
abstract: Question: did British ectomycorrhizal (ECM) fungal communities recover more where nitrogen (N) deposition decreased more? Data: 2.25 million FRDBI and CATE volunteer records from the NBN Atlas, counted per 10-km square in 1986-1999, 2000-2011 and 2012-2025; FungalTraits genus lifestyles and ECM exploration types; CBED deposition 1986-2012; CRU TS temperature. Planned test (written before outcomes): binomial models with square effects, period x 100-km-square effects and a period x deposition-change term, errors clustered on 50-km blocks. Result: the share of N-sensitive hydrophobic ECM types did not increase more where N decreased more: -0.006 log-odds per kg N/ha/yr (95% CI -0.038 to +0.026; 363 squares). Variants and the ECM share of all records gave the same result. But this indicator also had no N gradient inside regions in 1986-1999, so the planned null result is a weak test. Post hoc, we estimated species N niches in one half of the 50-km blocks and scored a community N index in the other half. ECM communities shifted with the local deposition change by 0.68 of their held-out spatial slope (bootstrap CI -0.15 to 1.86); saprotroph communities did not (-0.55, CI -1.44 to 0.07); the ECM minus saprotroph difference was 1.22 (CI 0.23 to 2.68). No shift occurred by 2000-2011. NHx, NOx and SOx changes could not be separated. Limitations: opportunistic records, 10-km exposure, no tree-cover control, CBED ends in 2012, post-hoc index. NBN data are CC BY-NC and are not bundled; a retrieval script and snapshot hashes are included.

Post-hoc community N index: tracking ratio (temporal slope / held-out spatial slope) with 50-km block bootstrap 95% CI; 1 means full tracking.
